variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Prometheus is a monitoring system that collects timestamped measurements and stores them as labeled time series. The Prometheus server discovers targets, periodically scrapes their HTTP metrics endpoints, writes samples to its local time-series database (TSDB), answers PromQL queries, and evaluates recording and alerting rules.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Core invariant”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Target
pairs.detail: An endpoint discovered from static configuration, Kubernetes, cloud APIs, files, DNS, or another supported service-discovery source.
pairs.explanation: An endpoint discovered from static configuration, Kubernetes, cloud APIs, files, DNS, or another supported service-discovery source.

pairs.label: Series
pairs.detail: A metric name plus one exact set of labels.
pairs.explanation: A metric name plus one exact set of labels. Changing any label value creates a different series identity.

pairs.label: Sample
pairs.detail: A float or native-histogram value associated with a timestamp inside one series.
pairs.explanation: A float or native-histogram value associated with a timestamp inside one series.

pairs.label: Rule
pairs.detail: A PromQL expression evaluated on an interval to create a recording series or an alert state.
pairs.explanation: A PromQL expression evaluated on an interval to create a recording series or an alert state.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Core invariantEvery unique metric-name and label-set combination is a separate time series, and every active series produces another sample on each successful scrape.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Target: An endpoint discovered from static configuration, Kubernetes, cloud APIs, files, DNS, or another supported service-discovery source. Series: A metric name plus one exact set of labels. Sample: A float or native-histogram value associated with a timestamp inside one series. Rule: A PromQL expression evaluated on an interval to create a recording series or an alert state.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Design the metric identity before instrumenting code”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Counter
pairs.detail: Tracks events that only increase until process restart, such as requests or failures.
pairs.explanation: Tracks events that only increase until process restart, such as requests or failures. Use rate() or increase() over a range instead of alerting on the raw total.

pairs.label: Gauge
pairs.detail: Moves up and down, such as queue depth, in-flight work, or available capacity.
pairs.explanation: Moves up and down, such as queue depth, in-flight work, or available capacity. Do not apply counter-reset logic to a gauge.

pairs.label: Histogram
pairs.detail: Records count, sum, and bucket observations.
pairs.explanation: Records count, sum, and bucket observations. Bucket boundaries determine both the series cost and which latency or size questions can be answered.

pairs.label: Summary
pairs.detail: Can expose count, sum, and configured quantiles.
pairs.explanation: Can expose count, sum, and configured quantiles. Precomputed quantiles generally cannot be aggregated across instances the way histogram buckets can.

variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Counter: Tracks events that only increase until process restart, such as requests or failures. Gauge: Moves up and down, such as queue depth, in-flight work, or available capacity. Histogram: Records count, sum, and bucket observations. Summary: Can expose count, sum, and configured quantiles.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose durability and availability per path”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Keep scrapes autonomous
pairs.detail: Run Prometheus close to its targets so a central-network failure does not erase all local visibility.
pairs.explanation: Run Prometheus close to its targets so a central-network failure does not erase all local visibility. Give each replica independent discovery and storage.

pairs.label: Protect local continuity
pairs.detail: Use supported local filesystems, disk alerts, tested snapshots where needed, and a retention-size limit that leaves filesystem headroom.
pairs.explanation: Use supported local filesystems, disk alerts, tested snapshots where needed, and a retention-size limit that leaves filesystem headroom.

pairs.label: Duplicate critical alerts
pairs.detail: Send each Prometheus replica directly to every Alertmanager instance.
pairs.explanation: Send each Prometheus replica directly to every Alertmanager instance. Do not hide the Alertmanager set behind a load balancer.

pairs.label: Define the remote contract
pairs.detail: Decide whether remote storage provides longer retention, global query, disaster recovery, or all three, then test backlog and replay behavior explicitly.
pairs.explanation: Decide whether remote storage provides longer retention, global query, disaster recovery, or all three, then test backlog and replay behavior explicitly.

variants.prompt: A Prometheus server scrapes 400 targets, each exposing 1,500 post-relabel series. How many active series does the model budget?
variants.explanation: Active series equals targets multiplied by series per target: 400 x 1,500 = 600,000.

options: It exposes cumulative bucket series plus count and sum series
